fields.label: Top row height
fields.help: The burger, the icons and their little counts are all sized from this, so a taller row makes them bigger instead of leaving them adrift in it. Below about 39px the three icons become small enough to fit beside the shop name instead of sitting on a line of their own, and the whole header shortens by about 50px at once — measured on a 360px screen; a wider phone crosses over lower.

fields.label: Scale the wordmark with it

fields.label: Placeholder

fields.label: Cart and wishlist count

tabs.label: Where it shows
tabs.description: One bar, two pages, two switches. The cart ships off so that page is untouched until you say otherwise.

fields.label: Show it on the checkout
fields.help: The bar under the Payment section, at the foot of the checkout.

fields.label: Show it on the cart page
fields.help: Off, so the cart page is exactly as it is today until you turn this on. It is the same bar with the same words — there is no second set to keep in step.

tabs.label: On a phone
tabs.description: The same bar at 900px and below, with its own shape. Ruled rows is what ships here and spread-to-both-edges is what ships on a desktop, which is the pair the owner chose; the switch at the top hands the phone back to the desktop's settings.

fields.label: Give the phone its own shape
fields.help: On, because a bar that reads as one line on a desktop reads as a scramble at 390px. Everything below is read only while this is on; with it off the phone gets the desktop's settings exactly as it always did.

fields.label: Shape on a phone
fields.help: At 900px and below.

options.bar: One line — everything on a single row
options.split: Two columns — brand on one side, contact on the other
options.stack: Stacked — brand, then help, then the links
options.rows: Ruled rows — each block on its own line, with a hairline between

fields.label: Alignment on a phone
fields.help: At 900px and below.

fields.label: Space above the bar on a phone
fields.help: Its own value, because a gap that reads right under a 1240px page is usually too much under a 390px one.

fields.label: Height on a phone
fields.help: Padding above and below together, at 900px and below. The two under it override it one at a time.

fields.label: Padding inside the top, on a phone
fields.help: Between the top edge of the bar and its first row. This is the one to reach for when the bar sits too close to the Place order box above it.

fields.label: Padding inside the bottom, on a phone
fields.help: And under the last row.

fields.label: Padding inside each row on a phone
fields.help: Ruled rows is the shipped phone shape, so this is the control that decides how tall the bar is there. 7 is what it worked out from the phone block gap before.

fields.label: Smallest row height on a phone
fields.help: A floor under each ruled row. 44 is the touch-target minimum if you want every row tappable.

fields.label: Side padding on a phone
fields.help: Between the screen edge and the first word. 20 lines the bar up with the checkout's own page padding.

fields.label: Space between blocks on a phone
fields.help: Between the brand, the help line, the contacts and the links.

fields.label: Text size on a phone
fields.help: A multiplier on 12px, at 900px and below.

tabs.label: Shape & size
tabs.description: Four structures and four alignments, which is sixteen looks from two controls. "One line" left-aligned is the shortest, and is what ships.

fields.label: Shape
fields.help: The structure. All four carry the same words; what changes is how they are grouped. Pair it with Alignment below.

options.bar: One line — everything on a single row
options.split: Two columns — brand on one side, contact on the other
options.stack: Stacked — brand, then help, then the links
options.rows: Ruled rows — each block on its own line, with a hairline between

fields.label: Alignment
fields.help: Where the content sits across the bar. "Spread to both edges" pushes the first block hard left and the last hard right, with the gap taken up in the middle — the classic footer look, and the one that reads worst when there are only two blocks left.

fields.label: Background
fields.help: Tones from the shop's own palette rather than a colour box: a footer that can be set to anything is a footer that can be set to something unreadable.

options.pink: Blush — the shop's own soft pink

fields.label: Line above the bar
fields.help: A hairline between the page and the footer. Off on the dark tone usually reads better, because the colour already separates them.

fields.label: Line thickness
fields.help: Only while the line above is on.

fields.label: Rounded top corners
fields.help: Rounds the two top corners, which lifts the bar off the page rather than sitting it flush. Works best with a tone that is not the page's own.

fields.label: Lift it off the page
fields.help: A soft shadow above the bar. It reads as a separate surface rather than as the end of the page — worth it with a rounded or contrasting tone, and usually not otherwise.

fields.label: Space above the bar
fields.help: Between the last block on the page and the top of the bar. The page's own background shows through it, so it reads as a gap rather than as more footer.

fields.label: Height
fields.help: Padding above and below together. The two controls under it override this one at a time; leave them alone and the bar is symmetric, as it was.

fields.label: Padding inside the top
fields.help: Between the top edge of the bar and its first line. Left where it is, it follows "Height" above.

fields.label: Padding inside the bottom
fields.help: And under the last line. Left where it is, it follows "Height" above.

fields.label: Padding inside each row
fields.help: Above and below each row of the "Ruled rows" shape, and the space the hairline sits in. 9 is what the shape worked out from the block gap before this had a number of its own.

fields.label: Smallest row height
fields.help: A floor under each ruled row, whatever the padding says. Zero is the row taking exactly the height of its words; 44 is a comfortable tap target on a phone.

fields.label: Side padding
fields.help: Between the screen edge and the first word.

fields.label: Content width
fields.help: Where the words stop. The bar itself always runs the full width of the window.

options.page: Line it up with the page above it
options.fixed: A width of my own, set below

fields.label: That width
fields.help: Read only while "A width of my own" is chosen above.

fields.label: Where the policy links sit
fields.help: Only the one-line shapes have a choice here; the stacked and ruled-row shapes put every block on its own line anyway.

options.brand: Under the wordmark, with the byline
options.inline: At the end of the row

fields.label: Space between blocks
fields.help: Between the brand, the help line, the contacts and the links. On a phone they wrap, and this is the gap on both axes.

fields.label: Text size
fields.help: Everything in the bar except the brand, which has its own size below. A multiplier on 12px.

fields.label: The wordmark
fields.help: The header's own logo, colours and weight — read live from Appearance → Header, so the two cannot drift apart.

fields.label: Brand size
fields.help: The wordmark alone. A multiplier on 14px.

fields.label: Brand in capitals
fields.help: On is the wordmark as it reads today. Off leaves whatever capitalisation is typed into the brand field.

fields.label: The mark beside the phone
fields.help: The glyph is WhatsApp's either way. This is whether it is drawn in the bar's own ink or in WhatsApp green.

options.mono: The bar's own colour — what it does today

fields.label: Separator between blocks
fields.help: A mark in the space between the brand, the help line, the contacts and the links. Drawn only on the one-line shapes, where blocks sit side by side and a separator has somewhere to go.

fields.label: Marks beside the phone and email
fields.help: The small WhatsApp and envelope glyphs. Off leaves the number and the address as plain text, which is shorter and quieter.

fields.label: Back-to-top arrow
fields.help: A small arrow at the far end of the bar. It scrolls the page rather than jumping, and it is hidden from screen readers only if it has no label.

fields.label: Arrow style
fields.help: How the arrow is drawn.

tabs.label: Content
tabs.description: Every word in the bar. Anything left empty is not drawn at all, rather than drawn empty — so the bar can be as short as a brand and a phone number.

fields.label: Brand name
fields.help: Drawn only while "The wordmark" above is set to the typed name. Leave it empty to draw no brand at all.

fields.label: Under the brand
fields.help: The company line. Empty draws nothing.

fields.label: Help heading
fields.help: Empty draws nothing.

fields.label: Help line
fields.help: Empty draws nothing.

fields.label: Phone shown
fields.help: Exactly as it should read. Empty removes the phone and its mark.

fields.label: Phone link
fields.help: Where tapping the number goes — a wa.me link for WhatsApp, or tel: to dial. Only http, https, tel and mailto links are accepted; anything else is drawn as plain text rather than as a link.

fields.label: Email shown
fields.help: Empty removes the email and its mark. It is linked with mailto: automatically.

fields.label: First link
fields.help: Empty removes the link.

fields.label: First link goes to
fields.help: A path on this shop, or a full https:// address.

fields.label: Second link
fields.help: Empty removes the link.

fields.label: Second link goes to
fields.help: A path on this shop, or a full https:// address.

fields.label: Third link
fields.help: Empty, so no third link is drawn. Returns and refunds is the usual one.

fields.label: Third link goes to
fields.help: A path on this shop, or a full https:// address.

fields.label: Small print
fields.help: A last line under the rest — a copyright, a licence number, a registered address. Empty draws nothing at all.

fields.label: Arrow label
fields.help: Read out by a screen reader; never shown. Empty hides the arrow from screen readers entirely, which is right only if the page has another way back up.

tabs.label: Payment marks
tabs.description: Off by default. The drawings themselves are a hardcoded constant — these switches only decide which of the six is printed.

fields.label: Show the payment marks
fields.help: A row of scheme marks in the bar. Off by default — it is a claim about what this shop accepts, so it is worth turning on deliberately and switching off the ones that are not true.

fields.label: Visa
fields.help: Only drawn while the row above is on.

fields.label: Mastercard
fields.help: Only drawn while the row above is on.

fields.label: Apple Pay
fields.help: Only drawn while the row above is on.

fields.label: Google Pay
fields.help: Only drawn while the row above is on.

fields.label: Tabby
fields.help: Only drawn while the row above is on.

fields.label: Tamara
fields.help: Only drawn while the row above is on.

tabs.label: Layout
tabs.description: Which cart page this shop serves, and whether it carries the site footer.

fields.label: Cart page layout
fields.help: Classic is the page as it is today. Squeezed is the docked-bar layout: dense product rows, a full-width recommended rail, the minimal coupon box and the two sticky rows at the foot of the screen.

options.classic: Classic — the page as it is today

fields.label: Show the site footer on the cart page
fields.help: Off, as asked: the cart page ships with no footer at all. THE CART PAGE ONLY — the footer still appears on the homepage, on product pages, on /shop/ and on every other page of the shop, and this switch cannot affect them. Turn it on to bring the footer back to the cart page; it applies to both the classic and the squeezed cart layouts.

tabs.label: Product rows
tabs.description: One height drives the whole line. Everything in it is worked out from that number.

fields.label: Row height
fields.help: The single control for how dense the basket is. The thumbnail, the type sizes and the quantity stepper are all worked out from it, so they shrink with the row instead of overflowing it.

fields.label: Text size in rows
fields.help: A nudge multiplied INTO the size the row height already produced, never an override — so this slider and the one above can never fight, and neither can silently win.

fields.label: Bold text in rows
fields.help: On is what the rows do today. Off gives every line regular weight.

fields.label: Size of the − / + quantity stepper
fields.help: The minus, the plus and the number between them. A multiplier and not a fixed size: the stepper is worked out from the row height like everything else in the line, so it still shrinks when you shorten the row — this nudges that result up or down. The digit scales with the box, so it stays centred at every setting.

tabs.label: Recommended
tabs.description: Full width, no rounded corners, no padding box around it.

fields.label: Show the recommended rail
fields.help: Renders nothing at all until products are chosen below, so this can stay on in a shop that has not picked any.

fields.label: Products across the screen
fields.help: In tenths: 45 is four and a half cards. The half card is the point — a card cut off by the screen edge is what tells a thumb there is more to the right. Card width is a fraction of the screen, so the count holds on every phone.

fields.label: Bold product names in the rail
fields.help: Off, as asked. The price below the name has its own switch — until you move that one it follows this.

fields.label: Bold prices in the rail
fields.help: Follows the product-name switch above until you move it. From then on it is its own setting and the two are independent.

fields.label: Line height of product names
fields.help: How far apart the two lines of a product name sit. The name is clamped to two lines and the box is worked out from this, so a looser setting gives the second line room rather than cutting it off.

fields.label: Space under the product name
fields.help: The gap between the name and the price under it.

fields.label: Space under the picture
fields.help: The gap between the product picture and the name under it.

fields.label: Size of the + button
fields.help: A multiplier on the one-tap add button, not a pixel size: the button is worked out from the screen width like the rest of the card, so it stays in proportion on every phone and this nudges that result.

fields.label: Move the + left or right
fields.help: Zero leaves it on the corner of the picture. Positive pushes it further out past that corner, negative tucks it back inside. It is measured from the corner it sits on, so it mirrors in a right-to-left shop.

fields.label: Move the + up or down
fields.help: Zero leaves it on the corner of the picture. Positive lifts it, negative drops it.

fields.label: Background movement
fields.help: The rail sits on a slow wash of colour. 0 holds it still. It is directly above the checkout button, so it is deliberately quiet — and it stops entirely for anyone whose phone asks for reduced motion.

tabs.label: Summary & trust
tabs.description: The figures under the coupon box, and the row of marks below them.

fields.label: Express Delivery Charge row
fields.help: Off, because this shop does not offer express delivery yet. THE EXPRESS FIGURE IS NEVER ADDED TO THE TOTAL even when this is on: the reference shows it priced beside a free Standard and a total that matches Standard, so it is an option a shopper picks at checkout, not a charge applied behind them.

fields.label: Express delivery charge
fields.help: Quoted, not added. See the switch above.

fields.label: Express (i) note
fields.default: Delivered the next working day where available. Chosen at checkout.
fields.value: Delivered the next working day where available. Chosen at checkout.

fields.label: Standard Delivery row
fields.help: Off, so the cart page does not try to answer a question the checkout answers properly. While it is off, the shop's own free-delivery bar takes its place in the summary — the green congratulations once an order qualifies, and how much more would qualify it before that.

fields.label: Standard (i) note
fields.default: Free on every order. Two to four working days.
fields.value: Free on every order. Two to four working days.

fields.label: Line shown when there is no free-delivery threshold
Service Fee row
fields.help: Off, and while it is off no fee is charged either — the row and the money are one switch, not two.

fields.label: Service fee · percentage
fields.help: Worked out on the order value AFTER any coupon, so a discount reduces the fee with it.

fields.label: Size of the trust row
fields.help: The tick, the wording and the payment marks together — they are one line, so one number moves all of it.

tabs.label: Docked rows
tabs.description: The two rows that stay at the foot of the screen.

fields.label: Text in both rows
fields.help: Everything in both docked rows is a multiple of this, so no wording can outgrow the bar it sits in.

fields.label: Space under the checkout row
fields.help: Extra white space below the docked rows. Zero is where they sit today, on the bottom edge. On a phone with a home indicator this is added to the space the hardware already reserves, not used instead of it.

fields.label: Text in the delivery row
fields.help: The delivery row only — its wording, the address under it and the button on the right. Multiplied into the size "Text in both rows" already produced, so this and that slider stack rather than overrule one another, and the checkout row below is left where it is.

fields.label: Weight of the delivery row text
fields.help: The heading — "Please choose your delivery address", and "Delivering to Home" once one is picked. Medium is what the row is today. The address line under it stays regular; the button has its own setting below.

fields.label: Address button text size
fields.help: The "+ Address" / "Change address" button only. Multiplied into the size "Text in both rows" already produced, so the two sliders stack rather than overrule one another.

fields.label: Weight of the address button
fields.help: The "+ Address" / "Change address" button only. Semi-bold is what it is today.

fields.label: Checkout button wording
fields.help: It shares the docked row with the item count and the total, so a longer word here is a narrower tally beside it. The button gives way first and ends in an ellipsis rather than pushing the figures off a 360px screen.

fields.label: Address row · once chosen
fields.help: Use {tag} where Home or Office should appear.

tabs.label: Desktop
tabs.description: The two-column cart page, from 1024px up. Everything here is read only on desktop — none of it can reach a phone.

fields.label: Two-column layout on desktop
fields.help: From the width below, the basket and the Recommended rail take the left column and everything else moves to the right. Off, a desktop gets the phone layout stretched across the screen, which is what it did before this existed.

fields.label: Desktop starts at
fields.help: Screens narrower than this keep the phone layout exactly as it is. 1024 leaves an iPad in portrait (768px) on the phone layout, which is the right call: two columns need room.

fields.label: Widest the page will go
fields.help: The two columns stop growing here and centre themselves. A basket row stretched across a 27-inch monitor is unreadable.

fields.label: Products across the rail
fields.help: In tenths: 55 is five and a half cards. The half card is deliberate — it is what tells someone the rail carries on past the edge. Desktop only; the phone keeps its own count under Recommended.

fields.label: Carousel arrows on the rail
fields.help: A round button at each end of the Recommended rail. Desktop only; a phone swipes instead, and the half card already tells it there is more.

fields.label: Quantity buttons on desktop
fields.help: Multiplied into the size "Product rows" already produced, so the phone keeps its own number and this adjusts it for desktop.

fields.label: Page side padding
fields.help: Space between the edge of the page and the columns.

fields.label: Space between sections
fields.help: Between the basket and the Recommended rail on the left, and between the summary and the checkout block on the right.

fields.label: Padding inside a section
fields.help: Inside the basket card, the rail and the summary — the space between a section's border and what it holds.

fields.label: Padding inside the checkout box
fields.help: The box holding the delivery address and Proceed to Checkout. It has its own number because it is the only section that is mostly a button.

fields.label: Right column follows the scroll
fields.help: The summary and Proceed to Checkout stay on screen while a long basket scrolls past. Off, they sit at the top and scroll away with the page.

fields.label: Gap above it when it sticks
Address popup width
fields.help: On a phone the address popup rises from the bottom edge. On desktop there is no bottom edge worth rising from, so it is a panel centred over the page.

tabs.label: Address popup
tabs.description: Its two heights — one for the list, a taller one for the form — its density and every word in it.

fields.label: New-address popup height · upright
fields.help: The popup that holds the FORM — the one with the fields in it. It grows from the bottom to fit what is in it and stops here. THE POPUP ITSELF NEVER SCROLLS — if a long address list would not fit, the list scrolls inside its own box and the Home / Office / Deliver here row stays put at the bottom where a thumb can reach it.

fields.label: Address-list popup height · upright
fields.help: The popup that holds the SAVED LIST — the one that opens first for a signed-in shopper who already has an address. Shorter than the form above it, because choosing needs less room than typing. Past this the list scrolls inside its own box; the popup itself still never does, so + Add New Address stays where a thumb can reach it.

fields.label: New-address popup height · on its side
fields.help: Used when the phone is held horizontally. The fields go two across and the address list goes two across at the same time.

fields.label: Address-list popup height · on its side
fields.help: The list popup, held sideways. It keeps a cap of its own there too — the landscape rule that widens the form to two columns widens the list to two columns as well, so the list needs LESS height on its side, not the same as the form.

fields.label: Blur behind the popup
fields.help: The page behind is frozen as well as dimmed while the popup is open, and that is not decoration: without the freeze a finger that misses the sheet scrolls the cart underneath it, and the address you were about to tap has moved by the time you tap again. Zero leaves the dimming and drops the blur.

fields.label: Show loading placeholders
fields.help: Grey blocks in the shape of what is coming, with a shimmer, while the shop is waiting on the server — opening the address popup, applying a coupon, changing a quantity. They appear only when a real request is in flight: a placeholder that flashes for a fortieth of a second reads as a glitch.

fields.label: City and Country on one row
fields.help: Applies when the phone is held upright. Held sideways the popup already puts every field two across, so this changes nothing there.

fields.label: Back-to-the-list link
fields.help: Top right of the address form, beside the close button. Shown only when there are saved addresses to go back to.

fields.label: Field · area · example
fields.help: Grey placeholder text, not a value. It disappears the moment anybody types.

fields.label: Note under the fields
fields.help: Singular, because only the country is filled in. A note that claims to have filled a field it left blank is a note nobody believes twice.
fields.default: Country set from where you are. Change it if it is wrong.
fields.value: Country set from where you are. Change it if it is wrong.

fields.label: Read out while the popup is loading
If the address cannot be saved
fields.default: That could not be saved. Please try again.
fields.value: That could not be saved. Please try again.

fields.label: Under the list · not signed in
fields.help: Only shown to a shopper who has not signed in and already has three. Signed-in addresses are saved to the account and are not capped.
fields.default: We keep your 3 most recent addresses on this device. Adding another replaces the oldest.
fields.value: We keep your 3 most recent addresses on this device. Adding another replaces the oldest.

tabs.label: Desktop · Layout
tabs.description: The two-column checkout, from 901px up. Nothing on this tab can reach a phone.

fields.label: Space above the header
fields.help: Between the top of the window and the secure-checkout bar. It was 52px and nobody chose it — a site-wide `section` rule reached in. Zero is the page with the band gone.

fields.label: Space below the page
fields.help: The other half of the same inherited rule, under the last block on the page. The page already carries its own bottom padding, so this was 52px of nothing.

fields.label: Page width
fields.help: How wide the whole checkout may grow on a large screen. Both columns and the gap between them live inside this. 1040 is the width the page has today.

fields.label: Summary column width
fields.help: The right-hand order summary. The form column takes whatever is left, so widening this narrows the form rather than widening the page.

fields.label: Space between the two columns
fields.help: The gutter between the form and the summary.

fields.label: Page padding — sides
fields.help: Breathing room between the page edge and the columns. On a screen wider than the page width above, this sits inside the centred block and does not move it.

fields.label: Page padding — top
fields.help: The gap under the secure-checkout header.

fields.label: Space between blocks
fields.help: Between the heading and the coupon box, and between the coupon box and the card that holds the four numbered sections.

fields.label: Padding inside each section
fields.help: Applies to all four numbered sections at once — Contact, Shipping address, Delivery and Payment. Their heading bars are worked out from this number, so the bars keep meeting the card edge at every value instead of drifting away from it.

fields.label: Padding inside the summary
fields.help: The right-hand column only.

fields.label: Summary follows the scroll
fields.help: On is what the page does today: the summary stays in view while the form scrolls past it. Off leaves it at the top of the column.

fields.label: Summary stops at
fields.help: How far below the top of the window the summary parks itself once it has caught up. Only read while the switch above is on.

tabs.label: Desktop · Header
tabs.description: The secure-checkout bar across the top. Its height is its padding plus the taller of the logo and the badge, so those are the controls rather than a "height" that would fight them.

fields.label: Header padding — top and bottom
fields.help: Together with the logo size below, this is the height of the bar: the bar is its padding plus the taller of the logo and the secure badge.

fields.label: Header padding — sides
fields.help: How far the logo sits from the left edge of the header block, and the badge from the right.

fields.label: Header width
fields.help: The band the logo and badge are laid out in — NOT the white bar, which always runs the full width of the window. Below the window width it pulls the logo and badge towards the middle; above it, it stops having anything left to give.

fields.label: Where the header band sits
fields.help: Only matters once the width above is narrower than the window.

options.page: Lined up with the page below it

fields.label: Logo size
fields.help: The "K-BeautyBliss" wordmark. The scroll offset that stops a focused field hiding under the bar is worked out from this and the padding above, so it follows them instead of staying at the number it was written with.

fields.label: Secure badge size
fields.help: The lock and the words beside it. The lock scales with the words.

fields.label: Header stays at the top while scrolling
fields.help: On is what the page does today. Off lets the bar scroll away with the rest of the page, which gives a phone back about 50px of screen.

tabs.label: Desktop · Text sizes
tabs.description: Every size is a share of the size that role already uses, so 100% is the page exactly as it is and the roles keep their relationship to each other.

fields.label: Page title size
fields.help: The word "Checkout" at the top of the form column — 19px today.

fields.label: Page subtitle size
fields.help: The line under the title — 12.5px today.

fields.label: Section heading size
fields.help: The four numbered bars — Contact, Shipping address, Delivery, Payment — 13px today. The round number in each one scales with it, so the bar keeps its shape.

fields.label: Field label size
fields.help: The small label above each field — 11px today — and with it the "(optional)" note and the wording of the tick-box lines.

fields.label: Field text size
fields.help: What the shopper types, and the placeholder before they do — 14px today.

fields.label: Placeholder size
fields.help: The grey hint inside an empty field — "First and last name", "you@email.com". A share of the field text above, so it follows that slider as well as this one.

fields.label: Trust line size
fields.help: The rating line and the authenticity line in the block under Payment — 12px today.

tabs.label: Desktop · Product rows
tabs.description: The lines in the order summary on the right — picture, name, stepper and price. Nothing on this tab can reach a phone, and nothing on it can reach the cart page.

fields.label: Space above the first line
fields.help: The quantity badge sits 7px above its picture, so on the first line it reaches above the list and gets cut. 8 clears it; 0 is the flush -- and clipped -- edge this page shipped with.

fields.label: Picture size
fields.help: The square thumbnail on each order-summary line, and with it the height of the line: the row is as tall as the picture until the picture is smaller than the name and stepper beside it. Drag this to squeeze the summary.

fields.label: Row padding — top
fields.help: Above each order-summary line. The first line in the list keeps its flush top edge at every value, so the summary never opens with a gap.

fields.label: Row padding — right
fields.help: Between the line price and the edge of the summary card. 0 is what the row has today.

fields.label: Row padding — bottom
fields.help: Below each line, above the divider.

fields.label: Row padding — left
fields.help: Between the edge of the card and the picture. 0 is what the row has today.

fields.label: Space between the picture and the text
fields.help: Only inside the line. The price stays pinned to the far edge.

fields.label: Text size in rows
fields.help: A nudge multiplied INTO the sizes the rows already use — the product name, the quantity figure and the line price together — never an override, so this and the picture size cannot fight and neither can silently win.

fields.label: Bold text in rows
fields.help: On is what the summary does today: a semibold name and a bold price. Off gives both a lighter weight without changing their sizes.

fields.label: Quantity stepper size
fields.help: The − and + buttons on each line, and the figure between them. A multiplier, so the control keeps its shape at every value instead of a bigger glyph rattling around in the same box.

fields.label: Remove button size
fields.help: The × on each order-summary line. It is 44×44 on a phone -- a full touch target, and the biggest single reason a phone line is taller than a desktop one. A multiplier, so the box and the glyph stay one shape.

fields.label: Tab height
fields.help: The floor under "Order summary" and "Browsed". Zero on a desktop, where the strip is sized by its padding alone.

fields.label: Tab padding
fields.help: Inside each of the two tabs, above and below the words. Together with the height above, this is how tall the strip is.

fields.label: Tab text size
fields.help: The words in both tabs, and the count badge beside "Browsed", which scales with them.

fields.label: Space below the tabs
fields.help: Between the tab strip and the first line of the right-hand summary.

tabs.label: Mobile · Layout
tabs.description: The single-column checkout, at 900px and below. Nothing on this tab can reach a desktop.

fields.label: Space above the header
fields.help: The phone half of the inherited `section{padding:52px 0}` — measured at 390px, the header sat 52px down the page for the same reason it did on a desktop. Zero is the band gone.

fields.label: Space below the page
fields.help: And the bottom half of it, under the Place order box.

fields.label: Page padding — sides
fields.help: The gap between the screen edge and every block on the page. The checkout is one column on a phone, so this is the page margin.

fields.label: Page padding — top
fields.help: The gap under the secure-checkout header.

fields.label: Space between stacked blocks
fields.help: The one column is a grid, and this is the gap between the summary at the top and the form below it.

fields.label: Space between blocks
fields.help: Between the heading and the coupon box, between the coupon box and the card of sections, and above the Place order box at the foot.

fields.label: Padding inside each section
fields.help: All four numbered sections, and the Place order box below them. Their heading bars follow it.

fields.label: Padding inside the summary
fields.help: The order-summary card at the top of the phone page.

fields.label: Floating Place order button
fields.help: A phone-only bar across the bottom carrying the total and a Place order button. Nothing on this row reaches a desktop.

options.off: Never — only the button in the page
options.smart: Only once the in-page button scrolls away
options.always: Always, from the moment the page loads

tabs.label: Mobile · Header
tabs.description: The same bar on a phone. Worth a look at 360px: the badge is the first thing that crowds the logo.

fields.label: Header padding — top and bottom
fields.help: Together with the logo size below, this is the height of the bar.

fields.label: Header padding — sides
fields.help: How far the logo sits from the screen edge, and the badge from the other one. Left where it is, it follows the page's own side padding so the logo lines up with everything below it; move it and it wins.

fields.label: Header width
fields.help: The band the logo and badge sit in. Anything at or above the phone's own width leaves them against the screen edges, which is what 1040 does — bring it down below about 360 to pull them in towards the middle.

fields.label: Where the header band sits
fields.help: Lined up is the default on a phone: a narrowed band used to centre itself, which put a notch to the left of the logo that nothing else on the page matched.

options.page: Lined up with the page below it

fields.label: Logo size
fields.help: The "K-BeautyBliss" wordmark.

fields.label: Secure badge size
fields.help: The lock and the words beside it. On a narrow phone this is the first thing that crowds the logo, so it is worth a look at 360px.

fields.label: Header stays at the top while scrolling
fields.help: On is what the page does today. Off gives a phone back the bar's height of screen, at the cost of the lock not being visible while someone types their card details.

tabs.label: Mobile · Text sizes
tabs.description: Same six roles, their own values. The field-text floor is the one control here that will not go below where it is, and it says why.

fields.label: Page title size
fields.help: The word "Checkout" at the top of the page — 19px today.

fields.label: Page subtitle size
fields.help: The line under the title — 12.5px today.

fields.label: Section heading size
fields.help: The four numbered bars — 13px today. The round number in each one scales with it.

fields.label: Field label size
fields.help: The small label above each field — 11px today — the "(optional)" note and the tick-box lines.

fields.label: Field text size
fields.help: What the shopper types — 16px on a phone today. Below 100% this does nothing while the floor below is on, which is how it ships; turn the floor off and the whole range works.

fields.label: Keep the 16px floor that stops iOS zooming
fields.help: On, as it ships. Off lets the slider above go all the way down — and lets iPhone Safari zoom the checkout in the moment a field is tapped, with no way for the shopper to zoom back out. If the aim is a smaller-looking field, the placeholder size below and the field padding on the Layout tab both get there without that.

fields.label: Placeholder size
fields.help: The grey hint inside an empty field. SAFE TO TAKE BELOW 100% on a phone: iOS decides whether to zoom the page from the field's own size, never the placeholder's, so this can go small while the field itself stays at the 16px that keeps the page still.

fields.label: Trust line size
fields.help: The rating line and the authenticity line in the block under Payment — 12px today.

tabs.label: Mobile · Product rows
tabs.description: The lines inside the summary card at the top of the phone page. Nothing on this tab can reach a desktop, and nothing on it can reach the cart page.

fields.label: Space above the first line
fields.help: The quantity badge sits 7px above its picture, so on the first line it reaches above the list and gets cut. 8 clears it; 0 is the flush -- and clipped -- edge this page shipped with.

fields.label: Picture size
fields.help: The square thumbnail on each order-summary line inside the collapsible summary card at the top of the phone page, and with it the height of the line.

fields.label: Row padding — top
fields.help: Above each line. The summary card shows about 148px before "View full summary", so squeezing this and the bottom fits more lines into that peek.

fields.label: Row padding — right
fields.help: Between the line price and the edge of the card. 0 is what the row has today.

fields.label: Row padding — bottom
fields.help: Below each line, above the divider.

fields.label: Row padding — left
fields.help: Between the edge of the card and the picture. 0 is what the row has today.

fields.label: Space between the picture and the text
fields.help: Only inside the line. The price stays pinned to the far edge.

fields.label: Text size in rows
fields.help: A nudge multiplied INTO the sizes the rows already use — the product name, the quantity figure and the line price together — never an override.

fields.label: Bold text in rows
fields.help: On is what the summary does today: a semibold name and a bold price. Off gives both a lighter weight without changing their sizes.

fields.label: Quantity stepper size
fields.help: The − and + buttons on each line, and the figure between them. Their 44px touch target is set separately and is not reduced by this, so a smaller stepper is still as easy to hit.

fields.label: Remove button size
fields.help: The × on each order-summary line. It is 44×44 on a phone -- a full touch target, and the biggest single reason a phone line is taller than a desktop one. A multiplier, so the box and the glyph stay one shape.

fields.label: Tab height
fields.help: The floor under "Order summary" and "Browsed". It ships at 44px -- a full touch target -- which is also what makes the strip 52px tall on a phone.

fields.label: Tab padding
fields.help: Inside each of the two tabs, above and below the words. Together with the height above, this is how tall the strip is.

fields.label: Tab text size
fields.help: The words in both tabs, and the count badge beside "Browsed", which scales with them.

fields.label: Space below the tabs
fields.help: Between the tab strip and the first line of the summary card at the top of the phone page.

tabs.label: Back to cart
tabs.description: The "Go back to cart" link at the top of the page — both surfaces on one tab. Which of the five LOOKS it wears is chosen on Store → Ecommerce → Checkout → Mobile layout; everything about its SIZE is here.

fields.label: Back-to-cart button size
fields.help: Scales the text and the padding of the "Go back to cart" link together, whichever of the five looks is chosen on Store → Ecommerce. 100% is the size it is today.

fields.label: Back-to-cart arrow size
fields.help: The chevron alone. Separate from the slider above because a smaller button usually wants a proportionally smaller glyph, not the same one.

fields.label: Back-to-cart corner radius
fields.help: Read only by the rounded-rectangle look. The pill looks are round by definition and the icon-only look is a circle.

fields.label: Back-to-cart button size
fields.help: The same link on a phone, its own value. 100% is today.

fields.label: Back-to-cart arrow size
fields.help: The chevron alone, on a phone.

fields.label: Back-to-cart corner radius
fields.help: The rounded-rectangle look only.

fields.label: Back-to-cart tap height
fields.help: The smallest the link may be on a phone, whatever the size slider says. 44px is the touch-target minimum; below it the link is harder to hit than it should be.

tabs.label: Trust & reviews
tabs.description: The stars and score above the order summary. The wording is yours; the figures are read from your approved reviews and cannot be typed. The authenticity lines — "100% authentic" beside the pay button and "100% authentic K-beauty" above the summary — are words about the business rather than about this page, so they live together with the rest of them on Store → Business Details → Claims.

fields.label: Show the reviews line
fields.help: The stars and the score above the order summary. It already draws nothing until there are enough approved reviews to mean anything, so this is for a shop that never wants it.

fields.label: Reviews line wording
fields.help: Use {rating} for the score and {count} for how many. Both are read from your approved reviews. Any OTHER digit is refused and the shipped wording is used instead — a number typed here would be a claim nobody earned, printed beside the pay button.

fields.label: Hide it below this many reviews
fields.help: Five is the shipped floor. One five-star review is true and is not a rating, which is why there is a floor at all.

tabs.label: Fields & attention
tabs.description: Which optional fields the page draws, and the two moving things on it: the cue that points at the address button while no address is chosen, and the authenticity tick under Payment. One set of values for both surfaces.

fields.label: Show the order-updates opt-in
fields.help: The tick under Contact — "Send me order updates and new offers". Off removes the row entirely, and nothing is recorded either way.

fields.label: Start it ticked
fields.help: Off, as asked: the shopper ticks it themselves. On restores the old behaviour, where the box arrived already ticked — which records a consent nobody actively gave, so it is worth being deliberate about.

fields.label: Show the delivery-notes box
fields.help: Off, as asked: the "Delivery instructions, a landmark, a preferred time" box under Delivery is not drawn. Turn it on to bring it back. Notes already saved on past orders are unaffected either way.

fields.label: Placeholder weight
fields.help: How heavy the grey hint inside an empty field is. Lighter reads as a hint; heavier reads as a value somebody typed, which is the thing a placeholder must never look like.

fields.label: Placeholder colour
fields.help: Against a white field. "Faint" is the quietest that still passes as readable text; anything quieter stops being a hint and starts being invisible, which is why there is no fainter option.

fields.label: Placeholder in italics
fields.help: Slanted, which separates the hint from what the shopper types more strongly than colour alone. Off is how it reads today.

fields.label: Point the shopper at the address button
fields.help: The icon pair, the moving arrow and the halo on the button, on the "choose your delivery address" row. Off leaves that row exactly as it was.

fields.label: Show the home and office icons
fields.help: A pair of overlapping marks at the start of the row — the same two the address popup uses — so the row reads as "an address goes here" before a word of it is read.

fields.label: Show the arrow pointing at the button
fields.help: A short dashed run and an arrowhead that travels along it towards Add address.

fields.label: Halo around the button
fields.help: A soft ring that grows and fades out from the button, roughly twice as slow as the arrow so the two read as one movement rather than a flicker.

fields.label: Animation speed
fields.help: Higher is faster. Everything moving in the cue is timed off this one number, so they keep step with each other at every value.

fields.label: Icon size
fields.help: The home and office marks and the arrow together.

fields.label: Animate the authenticity tick
fields.help: The shield under Payment draws its tick and fills green, pauses, and does it again.

fields.label: Tick speed
fields.help: Higher is faster. The pause between runs scales with it, so a slower tick also waits longer rather than drawing slowly and restarting at once.

tabs.label: Rules
tabs.description: When to hide Cash on delivery, and what to do when free delivery applies.

fields.name: cod_min
fields.label: Hide Cash on delivery below
fields.help: Zero means no lower limit.

fields.name: cod_max
fields.label: Hide Cash on delivery above
fields.help: Zero means no upper limit.

fields.name: hide_paid_free
fields.label: Only offer free delivery when it is available
fields.help: When an order already qualifies for free delivery, hide the paid delivery options instead of listing them beside it.

tabs.label: Pixels
tabs.description: Add an ID to activate that pixel. Leave any of them blank to skip it.

fields.name: meta_id
fields.label: Meta Pixel ID
fields.help: Fires PageView, ViewContent, InitiateCheckout and Purchase.

fields.name: ga4_id
fields.label: Google (GA4) Measurement ID
fields.help: Fires page_view, view_item, begin_checkout and purchase.

fields.name: tiktok_id
fields.label: TikTok Pixel ID
fields.help: Fires page browse and CompletePayment.
